From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure / FinBot

Hi Aiden, thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next steps to keep momentum.

Pain points you shared:
- Inference unit economics are the single biggest blocker to scaling (current cost per inference is ~4x what you're comfortable with).
- Latency spikes during peak traffic (95p sometimes > 400ms).
- Team lacks production-grade batching/caching in their stack; current approach is per-request single inference.

Current stack & constraints:
- Self-hosted models on AWS (g4dn/p3 family) with a custom inference wrapper.
- No quantization today; prioritized prediction quality over cost.
- Throughput needs: approx 300 reqs/sec average, spiky up to ~1.2k reqs/sec during business hours.

Success criteria you listed:
1) Reduce per-inference cost by ~3-4x without degrading quality beyond a small, agreed tolerance.
2) 95th percentile latency <= 200ms for our common request profile.
3) Clear rollout path (PoC -> pilot -> production) with measurable cost/latency improvements.

What Redwood can help with (summary):
- Optimizations: batching, KV/prefix caching, model quantization profiles, and autoscaled Dedicated pools for predictable throughput.
- Measurements: we'll run an initial cost model and a small PoC to demonstrate unit-economics improvements and latency SLOs.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) I'll send a simple cost-model spreadsheet and a short list of questions about your request distribution and token lengths. (attached)
2) Schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer to discuss quantization/phased rollout (our suggestion: start with INT8 or 4-bit quantization candidate models).
3) Mutual action plan draft and proposed pilot timeline (we'll draft after the deep-dive).

Attachments: redwood-cost-model.xlsx (spreadsheet/xlsx)

If that looks right, I'll send the calendar invite for the deep-dive later today.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa, this is helpful and accurate. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Our 4x number is an average across a mix of short and long prompts; the worst-case queries (longer chats) are much higher. If you can, please show both short-profile and long-profile cost projections in the spreadsheet.
- We're open to quantization but concerned about hallucination/regression risk; curious what your typical quality drop looks like at INT8 vs 4-bit.

Quick answers to your questions:
- Average token length: ~120 tokens; 80% of traffic is < 80 tokens, 20% is long-form (>250 tokens).
- Peak concurrency: We have spike windows at 10:00-11:00 and 15:00-15:30 PST, where tail latencies cause downstream retries.

Happy to join a 30-min deep-dive. Can do tomorrow (Wed) from 9-11am PT. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood requires model re-training to validate quantized models, or if you run compatibility tests without retraining?

Cheers,

Thanks for the details, Aiden — very helpful. A few short answers and an updated ask: 

- We'll add separate short/long profile tabs in the cost model and highlight tail token sensitivity. Expect an updated spreadsheet in ~2 hours.
- Quantization & quality: we typically run a calibration and regression test suite against your eval prompts. For many models, INT8 yields negligible quality drop on standard metrics; 4-bit can be very effective but sometimes requires per-layer calibration. We won't recommend retraining unless the regression tests show unacceptable deltas.

Proposed pilot approach:
1) Baseline capture: you share a 24-72 hour sample of traffic (anonymized) or a representative prompt set + label set for regression tests.
2) Redwood runs an offline quantization and regression pass against the sample, returns a quality report (diffs and example failures).
3) Run a small live PoC on Dedicated capacity with batching & caching enabled (2 weeks) to measure unit cost and tail latency.

Attachments: redwood-cost-model.xlsx (updated) ; FinBot_SLA_requirements.pdf (attachment stub, we referenced SLA specifics you shared).

Can you confirm: who from FinBot will own the sample export (SRE/ML eng)? Also I'll propose two slots for the deep-dive: Wed 10:00am PT or Wed 3:00pm PT, please pick one.

Best,
